name: Mauvette
lede: Mauvette is a very pale, pinkish lilac, a diminutive cousin of mauve.

sections.title: Little mauve
sections.body:
Paterson defines mauvette as a violet, purple or purplish pink [1]. In the entry just before it, mauve is traced to William Perkin's dye of 1856, first sold as aniline purple, and its French name to the streaks on the mallow flower [1]. The ending looks like a diminutive that would make mauvette a little mauve, though no book in our set says so.

The name sits in three historic systems in our records: Ridgway 1912 (plate XXV), ISCC-NBS 1955 (block 210), and Maerz and Paul 1930, which gives 1912 as its first record [2]. The scan of an aged Ridgway plate is approximate [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch is very light, with a lightness of 84 and low chroma [2]. Only 3 of 23,781 paintings cover 5% of their canvas with it, as photographed [3]. They include Bouguereau's *The Birth of Venus* (1879), about 26%, and Niels Larsen Stevns's view of Cagnes (1923), about 26% [3]. Its nearest standard name is [[thistle]], 2.7 ΔE away [2]. Related names: [[mauve]], [[mauvelous]], [[lilac]] and [[lavender]].
